items.prompt: What is the Sun?

options.why: A planet travels around a star.
A moon travels around a planet.

hints: There are millions of others far away.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star that gives out light and heat.

items.prompt: How many planets are in our Solar System?
hints: Count them from Mercury to Neptune.
items.explanation: There are eight planets in the Solar System.

items.prompt: Which planet is nearest to the Sun?

options.why: Neptune is the furthest planet.
Earth is the third planet.

items.explanation: Mercury is the planet nearest the Sun.

items.prompt: What do the planets travel around?

options.why: Only the Moon travels around the Earth.
The Moon travels around the Earth.

items.explanation: All the planets travel around the Sun.

items.prompt: Which planet is the furthest from the Sun?

options.why: Mercury is the nearest.
Mars is the fourth planet.

items.explanation: Neptune is the eighth and furthest planet from the Sun.

items.prompt: Put the first four planets in order, starting nearest the Sun.
items.explanation: The order from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.

items.prompt: Which of these is a planet?

options.why: Sirius is a star.
The Moon is a natural satellite.

items.explanation: Jupiter is the biggest planet in the Solar System.

items.prompt: The Sun is at the ___ of the Solar System.
items.explanation: The Sun is at the centre of the Solar System.

items.prompt: What is an asteroid?

options.text: a ball of ice and dust with a long tail
options.why: That describes a comet.

options.text: a lump of rock that travels around the Sun
a star that is very far away
options.why: Stars are not lumps of rock.

hints: Most are in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
They are made of rock or metal.
They are much smaller than planets.
items.explanation: Asteroids are lumps of rock that travel around the Sun.

items.prompt: What is a comet made of?

options.why: Comets are not on fire.
Comets are mostly ice and dust.

hints: It has a bright tail when near the Sun.
The tail is made of material that melts off.
items.explanation: A comet is a ball of ice and dust. Near the Sun it grows a bright tail.

items.prompt: Sort each object into the right group.
hints: Comets, asteroids and moons are not planets.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star, Mars and Saturn are planets, and comets, asteroids and moons are other objects.

items.prompt: Which of these are found in the Solar System?

options.text: stars that are billions of kilometres away
options.why: Other stars are outside the Solar System.
Other galaxies are far beyond the Solar System.

hints: The Solar System means the Sun and what travels around it.
Other stars are not part of it.
Planets and asteroids both travel around the Sun.
items.explanation: The Solar System has the Sun, planets, asteroids, comets and moons.

items.prompt: How are the four planets nearest the Sun different from the four furthest away?

options.text: The nearest four are made of gas and the furthest are rock.
options.why: It is the other way round.

options.text: The nearest four are small and rocky, and the furthest four are much bigger.
They are all the same size.
options.why: The planets are very different sizes.

items.explanation: The inner planets are small and rocky. The outer planets are giants made mostly of gas or ice.

items.prompt: What is a planetary system?

options.text: a group of planets with no star
options.why: A planetary system has a star at the centre.

options.text: a star with planets and other objects travelling around it
only the planets in our Solar System
options.why: Other stars can have planetary systems too.

hints: Our Solar System is one example.
It needs a star at the centre.
items.explanation: A planetary system is a star with planets and other objects travelling around it.

items.prompt: A ___ is a lump of rock that travels around the Sun.
hints: It is smaller than a planet.
Many are found between Mars and Jupiter.
items.explanation: An asteroid is a lump of rock that travels around the Sun.

items.prompt: Why does Mars look like a star in the sky?

options.text: It makes its own light like the Sun.
options.why: Planets do not make their own light.

options.text: It reflects sunlight and looks like a bright dot.

options.why: Planets are not burning.

hints: They look like bright dots at night.
items.explanation: Planets shine because they reflect sunlight. They do not make their own light.

items.prompt: Which statement about the Sun is correct?

options.why: The Sun is a star, not a planet.

options.text: It is the only star in our Solar System.

options.why: The Earth travels around the Sun.

hints: Look for a statement about it being a star.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star and the only one in the Solar System.

items.prompt: The Sun looks much bigger than other stars at night. What is the main reason?

options.text: It is the biggest star in the universe.
options.why: Many stars are far bigger than the Sun.

options.text: It is much closer to us.

options.why: It is a star.

hints: Other stars are trillions of kilometres away.
items.explanation: The Sun is our closest star, so it looks much bigger and brighter than the others.

items.prompt: A new planet is found travelling around a distant star. What would this be an example of?

options.text: a new Solar System that includes the Sun
options.why: It is a different star, not the Sun.
It does not travel around the Earth.

hints: It is a different star from the Sun.
A star with planets forms a system.
items.explanation: A star with planets travelling around it is a planetary system.

items.prompt: Which sentence best describes the Moon?

options.text: It is a small planet that travels around the Sun alone.
options.why: The Moon travels around the Earth.

options.text: It travels around the Earth and reflects sunlight.
It is a star that makes its own light.
options.why: The Moon does not make light.

hints: The Moon is not a planet or a star.
items.explanation: The Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth. It shines because it reflects sunlight.

items.prompt: True or false: The Sun is a star at the centre of our Solar System.
items.explanation: All the planets orbit it. The Sun is the only star in our Solar System.

items.prompt: True or false: Mars is the planet closest to the Sun.
hints: It is very small and hot.
items.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet. Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.

items.prompt: True or false: There are eight planets in our Solar System.
items.explanation: They are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

items.prompt: True or false: Jupiter is the smallest planet.
items.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System. Mercury is the smallest.
